opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Marketing the movies, shows and parks, and running the company.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: The wear and tear on parks, cruise ships and equipment, spread over their working lives.

opex.name: Restructuring & impairment charges
opex.note: Costs of reshaping parts of the business and writing down assets that lost value.

follow100Note: Of the $10.71 kept as profit per $100 of revenue, about $0.36 belongs to noncontrolling partners — $10.35 is Disney shareholders'. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Of the $2,644M of net income, $90M belongs to noncontrolling partners; $2,554M is attributable to Disney (the $1.40 EPS figure). Costs are split between services and products using the Q1 FY25 10-Q, since the earnings release reports one combined cost line; operating income of $3,935M is derived as revenue less those costs and the restructuring charge.
oneTimers: Restructuring and impairment charges were $143M in the quarter.
Disney's adjusted EPS of $1.76 excludes the restructuring charges and $397M of amortization from the TFCF (Fox) and Hulu acquisitions; GAAP EPS was $1.40.
otherDetail: Interest expense, net, of $367M on Disney's debt, partly offset by $92M of equity income from companies Disney part-owns — now including its 37% stake in the India joint venture formed with Reliance in November 2024.
segmentNote: Segment operating income: Entertainment $1,703M, Sports $247M, Experiences $3,110M (before corporate costs).

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Streaming subscriptions, TV networks and channels, park tickets and hotel stays — the large majority of Disney's money.

segments.name: Products
segments.note: Merchandise, food and drinks, and other things Disney physically sells.

takeaways.text: Experiences — parks, resorts and cruises — earned $3,110M of operating income, flat with a year ago at a very high level, on revenue up 3% to $9.4B. It remains Disney's biggest profit engine by far.
takeaways.title: Experiences stayed at full steam

takeaways.text: Entertainment operating income nearly doubled to $1,703M: Direct-to-Consumer swung to a $293M profit from a $138M loss, content sales jumped 34% on theatrical hits, and Sports recovered to $247M from a $103M loss.
takeaways.title: Streaming swung to profit

takeaways.text: Diluted EPS was $1.40, up 35%; excluding restructuring charges and acquisition amortization, adjusted EPS was $1.76, up 44%. Cash from operations rose 47% to $3.2B, though free cash flow was $739M after studio and parks spending.
takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS rose 44%

verdict: Disney grew revenue 5% to $24.7B and segment profit 31% to $5.1B — streaming swung to a $293M profit and content sales surged — leaving $2.6B of net income, up 23%.
